spec.paper_title: Seasonality in the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
spec.selected_experiment: Table 2, Years 2-5 Annual strategy: equal-weighted decile portfolios sorted on average returns at annual lags 24, 36, 48, and 60 months, held one month (10-1 winner-loser spread)

economic_rationale.value: Persistent seasonal variation in expected returns: individual stocks persistently earn different (relatively high or low) returns in specific calendar months, so stocks that did well in a given calendar month in past years tend to do well in that same calendar month again.

evidence.quote: This result is consistent with individual stocks that persistently earn different returns over

universe_and_filters.value: NYSE/AMEX-listed firms whose data is available on the CRSP monthly returns file; holding-period returns January 1965 through December 2002 (456 months), with lagged returns back to January 1945; only stocks available strictly before each date are used. No further filters stated.
